In [[geometry]], the '''gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda''' is a [[Johnson solid]], a convex polyhedron with thirty [[equilateral triangle]]s, six [[regular pentagon]]s, and one [[regular decagon]] as its faces.

== Construction ==
To construct, begin by attaching the [[pentagonal rotunda]]'s base to one of the [[pentagonal antiprism]]'s decagons. This construction is called [[gyroelongation]]. This replaces the [[regular decagon|decagon]] with ten [[equilateral triangle]]s and six [[regular pentagon]]s from the faces of a pentagonal rotunda. Hence, the faces of such a resulting polyhedron have thirty equilateral triangles, six regular pentagons, and one regular decagon, adding from the faces of a pentagonal antiprism, and the total number of faces is thirty-seven. Because both polyhedra are [[Convex polyhedron|convex]] and the faces are [[regular polygon]]s, the gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda is a [[Johnson solid]], enumerated as 25th Johnson solid <math> J_{25} </math>.<ref name="berman">{{cite journal
 | last = Berman | first = Martin
 | year = 1971
 | title = Regular-faced convex polyhedra
 | journal = Journal of the Franklin Institute
 | volume = 291
 | issue = 5
 | pages = 329–352
 | doi = 10.1016/0016-0032(71)90071-8
 | mr = 290245
}}</ref>

From this construction, the gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda is a [[composite polyhedron]].

== Properties ==
[[File:J25 gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda.stl|thumb|3D model of a gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda]]
A gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda has the same [[Point groups in three dimensions|three-dimensional symmetry group]] as the pentagonal rotunda, namely the cyclic group <math> C_{5\mathrm{v}} </math> of order ten. Its [[dihedral angle]], an angle between two polygonal faces, can be obtained from the dihedral angle of a pentagonal rotunda and of a pentagonal antiprism. There are five distinguishing dihedral angles:<ref name=johnson>{{cite journal
 | last = Johnson | first = Norman W. | author-link = Norman Johnson (mathematician)
 | doi = 10.4153/CJM-1966-021-8
 | journal = Canadian Journal of Mathematics
 | mr = 185507
 | pages = 169–200
 | title = Convex polyhedra with regular faces
 | volume = 18
 | year = 1966| s2cid = 122006114 | doi-access = free
 }} See Table III, line 6.</ref>
* the two triangle-to-decagon angles are around {{Val|142.6|u=deg}} and {{Val|158.7|u=deg}},
* the triangle-to-decagon angle is around {{Val|95.2|u=deg}}, from the angle between the triangular faces and the antiprism's base, and
* the two pentagon-to-triangle angles are around {{Val|174.4|u=deg}} and {{Val|159.2|u=deg}}.

The surface area of a gyroelongated pentagonal rotunda is obtained by adding all of the polygonal faces' areas, and the volume is obtained by summing the volume of a pentagonal rotunda and of a pentagonal antiprism. With edge length <math> a </math>, the surface area <math> A </math> and volume <math> V </math> are:{{r|berman}}<math display="block"> \begin{align}
 A & = \frac{1}{2}\left( 15\sqrt{3}+\left(5+3\sqrt{5}\right)\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{5}}\right)a^2 \approx 31.007a^2, \\
 V &= \left(\frac{45}{12}+\frac{17}{12}\sqrt{5} + \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{2\sqrt{650+290\sqrt{5}}-2\sqrt{5}-2}\right) a^3 \approx 13.667a^3
\end{align}</math>
